newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-TALL ORDER FOR AJAX IN DUTCH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TALL ORDER FOR AJAX IN DUTCH LEAGUE.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam need a miracle to close an 18-point gap on leaders PSV Eindhoven and win their fourth consecutive Dutch first division title.
With 18 matches to go as the season resumes at the weekend after the winter break, Ajax have 30 points from 20 matches and trail way behind PSV (48 points) and Feyenoord Rotterdam (45).
Ajax were beset by injury problems during the first half of the season.

Now the injuries have healed, the players must handle the uncertainty of changes to come. Coach Louis van Gaal will definitely leave at the end of the season and striker Partick Kluivert and defender Winston Bogarde have also indicated they will go.
Van Gaal will be replaced by former Danish international Morten Olsen next season. It is still unclear where Van Gaal will go, although he has said he has an agreement with a top European club.
It is also uncertain whether the De Boer twins Ronald and Frank will stay with Ajax, with English premier league Arsenal rumoured to have made them a generous offer.
Ajax have not made any big moves in the transfer market during the winter, acquiring only midfielder Dean Gorre from Groningen for next season.
Already out of the Dutch Cup and with the league title virtually out of reach, they have one main goal left this season: the European Cup.
Ajax reached the final in the past two seasons, winning the trophy in 1995 and losing to Italy's Juventus last year. They face Atletico Madrid in the quarter-finals in April.
PSV, whose performance has dipped after the winter break sometimes in the past, have onlyb one real problem.

They have signed striker Gilles de Bilde from Anderlecht but must reckon without him until next season because the Belgian has been suspended until the end of March after assaulting another player in a league game.
FIFA, soccer's world governing body, has said De Bilde cannot obtain a licence to play in the Netherlands until the suspension is over and by then the Dutch transfer period will have ended.
PSV coach Dick Advocaat was happy with first half of the season but remains cautious.
"On paper it all looks healthy but we still have to do it this season. The prizes will be handed out at the end of the season," the former Dutch national coach said.

Feyenoord have been preparing in South America and have brought back two new players -- Uruguayan defender Alvaro Picun de Leon, known as Fernando, and Argentine striker Eduardo "Tati" Bustos Montoya.
They now have four South American players on their books.
Feyenoord did better than expected at the start of the season when coach Arie Haan said he was building a team for the future and had no title aspirations.
On Sunday Ajax visit De Graafschap Doetinchem, dubbed the "Super Peasants". De Graafschap are the surprise package of the season and are fifth in the table with 33 points.
PSV travel to Vitesse Arnhem and Feyenoord visit mid-table Volendam.
